 The Mansfield campus of Commonwealth University would close by June 2028 under a plan announced by the Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education Tuesday morning.
 The Mansfield University campus is located North Central Pennsylvania. Read more Johnmaslar / Wikimedia Commons by Susan Snyder Published  Nov. 17, 2026, 9:56 a.m. ET Listen to article •   0:00 min For the first time in its 43-year history, the Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education plans to shut down one of its original 14 universities due to plummeting enrollment and a deficit.
 The Mansfield campus of Commonwealth University would close by June 2028 under a plan announced by the system Tuesday morning. Mansfield in 2022 was merged with Bloomsburg University and Lock Haven University into the Commonwealth University as PASSHE attempted to cope with declining enrollment.
 But that didn’t stave off enrollment declines. The campus, which enrolls just over 1,000 students, has lost 71.6% of its enrollment since 2009, and is expected to decline another 20% by 2028 to 802 students, according to PASSHE. The campus’ freshman to sophomore retention rate has also fallen to 60% this fall, the system said. That means 40% of freshmen who entered in fall 2025 didn’t return this fall.
 The campus ran a deficit of $7.7 million in 2025-26, and nearly 60% of its residence hall beds are empty this fall.
 » READ MORE: Merger of six Pennsylvania state universities gets OK, the biggest change in the system’s history 
 The PASSHE system until this point has been reluctant to close campuses, despite a 30% decline in overall enrollment since 2010, worrying it would leave some areas of the state unserved by higher education.
 “Planning now for an orderly wind-down of operations at the Mansfield campus will put Commonwealth University on a stronger path to long-term success and better position it to continue providing a relevant, rigorous and affordable education to students.” PASSHE Chancellor Christopher Fiorentino said in a statement. “Our top priority through this process is that students at the Mansfield campus have a path to finish their degree at Commonwealth University.”
 Fiorentino directed Commonwealth University President Jeffery Osgood to develop a plan for the closure and submit it by Dec. 8.
 “I understand how deeply people care about Mansfield and how difficult this will be for those who have dedicated years of their lives to the campus,” Fiorentino said. 
 But he said in a letter to Osgood that if the system continued to cover deficits it would have to come out of the reserves of the other universities.
 The plan will address how current students on the Mansfield campus will be able to continue to get their degrees from Commonwealth, he said.
 The move by PASSHE comes as Pennsylvania State University prepares to close seven of its Commonwealth campuses at the end of this academic year and signifies a continued shake up in the state’s higher education landscape amid falling enrollments. 
 Mansfield is among a growing string of Pennsylvania universities to close in recent years. The University of the Arts in Philadelphia abruptly shut in 2024 and Cabrini University also closed that year. Rosemont College plans to conclude operations by 2028; Pierce College recently merged into Lackawanna College. Earlier, the University of the Sciences was absorbed by St. Joseph’s University and Philadelphia University by Thomas Jefferson University .
 The PASSHE plan to shut Mansfield is subject to approval by the board of governors. It does not require state approval because it became a branch campus in 2022, not a stand alone university, PASSHE spokesperson Kevin Hensil said.
 The recommendation by Fiorentino to direct a wind down of operations at Mansfield followed analysis of enrollment, finances, regional demographics and infrastructure needs at Bloomsburg, Lock Haven and Mansfield that began in July.
